🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-10-03 23:00 → 2026-10-04 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Full verification loop closed on PR #59** — A cold-clone run reproduced all pins and vectors and killed every mutant, giving the implementation a clean bill of health before cross-evaluation. [tg:tawg:5219]

> **PRF PR #13 landed on main** — A new conformance profile capturing guarantee-transfer settlement reached main, turning a discussion artifact into a merged, testable fixture. [tg:tawg:5223]

> **Cross-evaluation schema ready for both artifacts** — With PR #14 drafted and pinned, both PR #59 and PRF #13 now have a neutral contract to run against, making the interoperability test concrete and actionable. [tg:tawg:5259]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### protected-relation-fixtures
_The conformance work moved from individual verification into a shared evaluation layer._

- Zexo (@zexoverz) **Verified** PR #59 at a specific commit on a cold clone, confirming that all test vectors reproduce and every mutant is killed, which removes implementation-integrity uncertainty before the group runs any cross-evaluation. [tg:tawg:5219]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Landed** PR #13 on main with the award-actual-settlement-v0 conformance profile, giving the group a concrete merged fixture that captures guarantee-transfer behavior in a form both sides can evaluate against. [tg:tawg:5223]
- Baby Blue Viper **Endorsed** the schema-first gate as the right interoperability criterion, framing the standard as: if both artifacts evaluate cleanly through one neutral contract without either native verdict bending to fit, that constitutes real evidence of compatibility. [tg:tawg:5244]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Opened** PR #14 with a draft schema and prototype pinned to a specific commit, providing the neutral evaluation surface that lets PR #59 and PRF #13 be tested together without importing either artifact's own assumptions. [tg:tawg:5259]

### guarantee-preservation
_The group converged on a principle-first, interface-level approach before any ERC commitment._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Proposed** a Guarantee Preservation Rule grounded in two concrete cases, drawing a precise line between checking declared dependencies and establishing that those dependencies actually hold — a conceptual anchor the group can build conformance criteria around. [tg:tawg:5239]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Advocated** staying at the conformance and interoperability layer rather than committing to an ERC draft early, keeping the interface shape provable before any spec locks the group in. [tg:tawg:5243]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Affirmed** the boundary-commitment framing — agreeing that no one should guess whether a scheme preserves soundness — which strengthens the shared standard for what counts as a valid preservation claim. [tg:tawg:5204]
- Petchevere (@petchevere) **Clarified** that the zkIE discussion is scoped tightly to the agent-action thread, preventing related but distinct lines of work from blurring and keeping the group's work streams cleanly separated. [tg:tawg:5194]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**
- Explore whether the Guarantee Preservation Rule can be expressed as a machine-checkable predicate at the conformance layer, before any ERC draft is written.
- Consider what a "native verdict bending" failure looks like in practice and whether the cross-evaluation schema in PR #14 can surface it reliably.

### ✅ **TODOs**
- Run PR #59 against the draft schema and prototype in PRF PR #14 to produce the first cross-evaluation result.
- Review whether the award-actual-settlement-v0 conformance profile in PR #13 satisfies the Guarantee Preservation Rule as proposed.
- Confirm that the agent-action and zkIE thread scoping stays clean as both discussions develop in parallel.

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A complete verification pass on one implementation fed directly into the opening of a neutral cross-evaluation schema — the group moved from "does this hold on its own?" to "can both artifacts clear a shared bar?" without pausing between the two steps.
>
> When the mutation suite goes 8-for-8 and the draft schema drops before the window closes, the hardest thing left is agreeing on the framing — which, honestly, is the good kind of hard. 🔬
